o1.biggest_strength: Puts the exact cash limit ('about 10 notes, laid flat') and the break-in note everywhere the buyer decides — under the button, in the bullet, in the FAQ — directly targeting the 44% cash returns and 7-day tight-slot returns.
o1.biggest_mistake: Leads the deliverable with a block of internal analytics rationale the customer will read; that belongs in a cover note, not on the product page.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the strategy rationale off the page into a separate note, tighten the description's voice, and add outer dimensions or a clearer front-pocket answer so Tom's 'will it fit in my pocket' doubt is fully closed.

Also leaves the button line as warranty rather than using it to cut break-in returns.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop or confirm the invented extra-note capacity, put the 'snug for a week' note under the add-to-cart line to cut returns, and lead the subtitle/bullets with the exact millimetre numbers up front.

reason: Both are usable and on-brief, but Output 1 attacks the return problem most precisely — the cash number and break-in note are placed everywhere the buyer decides, including the button — while Output 2 reads better but invents a capacity figure and wastes the add-to-cart line.
